Tony Lorenzo Delk was born on January 28, 1974.
Tony Delk is an American.
Tony Delk is a former professional basketball player and college assistant coach.
Tony Delk last served as an assistant coach for the New Mexico State Aggies men's basketball team.
During his playing days, Tony Delk was team leader of the Kentucky Wildcats that won the 1996 NCAA Championship Game.
After college, Tony Delk played for eight NBA teams over 10 seasons.
Tony Delk attended Haywood Junior High School in Brownsville, Tennessee.
Tony Delk attended Haywood High School in Brownsville, Tennessee.
In his senior year of high school, Tony Delk was named "Mr. Basketball" in the state of Tennessee (TSSAA Class 3A Mr.Basketball 1992).
In his senior year of high school, Tony Delk was also to the Parade and McDonald's All-American Teams.
Tony Delk's jersey hangs in Rupp Arena.
As a sophomore at Kentucky, Tony Delk was voted All-SEC 2nd Team by the coaches.
As a sophomore at Kentucky, Tony Delk was voted All-SEC 3rd Team by the Associated Press.
As a sophomore at Kentucky, Tony Delk made the All-SEC Tournament Team for his outstanding play.
During the 1994–95 season, Tony Delk was named to the All-SEC 1st and All-NCAA Regional teams.
During the 1995–96 season, Tony Delk was named to the All-American and All-SEC first teams.
During the 1995–96 season, Tony Delk was named NCAA basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player.
During the 1995–96 season, Tony Delk received SEC Player of the Year honors.
Tony Delk joined Omega Psi Phi Fraternity while at Kentucky.
Tony Delk was picked 16th overall in the 1996 NBA draft by the Charlotte Hornets.
Tony Delk was traded by the Hornets along with Muggsy Bogues to the Golden State Warriors for B. J. Armstrong on November 7, 1997.
Tony Delk played for two seasons with the Golden State Warriors.
Tony Delk signed with the Sacramento Kings on August 16, 1999.
In a January 2, 2001, overtime game against the Kings, Tony Delk scored a career-high 53 points on 20-for-27 field goal shooting.
This was the only game of Tony Delk's career in which he scored 30 or more points.
Tony Delk was eventually dealt with Rodney Rogers to the Celtics for Joe Johnson, Milt Palacio, and Randy Brown.
On October 20, 2003, Tony Delk was traded to the Dallas Mavericks along with Antoine Walker for Chris Mills, Jiří Welsch, Raef LaFrentz, and a 2004 first-round pick.
After a year with the Mavericks, Tony Delk and Walker were again traded in a deal for Jason Terry and Alan Henderson.
Tony Delk lasted one and a half seasons with the Hawks before being waived on February 25, 2006.
On March 1, 2006, Tony Delk signed with the Detroit Pistons to back up point guard Chauncey Billups.
Tony Delk finished his NBA career with averages of 9.1 PPG, 2.5 RPG and 1.9 APG.
In August 2006, Tony Delk signed a contract with the Greek basketball team, Panathinaikos in Athens.
Tony Delk won the Greek Cup with Panathinaikos.
Tony Delk won the Greek Championship with Panathinaikos.
Tony Delk won the European Championship with Panathinaikos.
On May 2007, Tony Delk was released from Panathinaikos citing compatibility issues.
In November 2007, Tony Delk announced his retirement from professional basketball.
In 2008, Tony Delk played three games for the Gigantes de Carolina in the BSN, the professional basketball league of Puerto Rico.
Tony Delk retired again and served as a technical assistant with the same team.

On April 16, 2009, it was announced that Tony Delk would be returning to his alma mater along with his former college teammate Scott Padgett to serve on coach John Calipari's staff at the University of Kentucky.
In July 2011, the New Mexico State Aggies basketball team hired Tony Delk as an assistant coach to Marvin Menzies.
In June 2013, Tony Delk left the New Mexico State staff to pursue other opportunities closer to his family in Atlanta.
In October 2014, the SEC Network announced that Tony Delk had been hired as an in-studio analyst and announcer for the upcoming college basketball season.
Tony Delk is the president of the Taylor Delk Sickle Cell Foundation.
The foundation is named after his daughter who has sickle cell disease.
Tony Delk divorced from his former wife, Margie Delk, in 2007.
